paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Israel didn't fall because Assyria was strong. The writer says it plainly: "All this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt" (2 Kings 17:7). The God who rescued them was the One they walked away from.

And He didn't stay quiet about it. The writer says "through all His prophets and seers, the LORD warned Israel and Judah, saying, 'Turn from your wicked ways and keep My commandments…'" (2 Kings 17:13). Warning after warning, and the writer says "they would not listen" (2 Kings 17:14). I've ignored my oven timer more than once, so I know how it goes: the warning was never the problem, the listening was.

So what does that mean for you, baker? When God speaks in His Word, it's a loving call to turn back, and it's worth hearing while there's still time to turn. Hearing Him and doing what He says is how we stay close to the God who brought us out. This story isn't over, either, because Judah is still standing, and what happens to them comes next.
